paper.title: The FDA-Approved and Non-FDA-Approved Indications for Biostimulatory Fillers off the Face.
paper.summary:
BACKGROUND: Biostimulatory fillers are increasingly used beyond the face to address age-related dermal thinning, laxity, crepiness, and soft-tissue volume loss through neocollagenesis and tissue remodeling.
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to review the use of calcium hydroxylapatite (CaHA) and poly-l-lactic acid (PLLA) for off-face rejuvenation, emphasizing indications, treatment techniques, clinical outcomes, and safety.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Published literature, consensus recommendations, and clinical experience regarding CaHA and PLLA were reviewed across multiple anatomic sites, including the hands, neck, décolletage, arms, forearms, breasts/chest wall, abdomen, buttocks, knees, and genital areas.
RESULTS: Both CaHA and PLLA improve skin quality, laxity, and soft-tissue support through collagen stimulation and dermal remodeling. Optimal outcomes depend on anatomic site, appropriate dilution, subdermal or subcutaneous placement, and meticulous injection technique. Combination approaches with energy-based devices and other regenerative treatments may enhance outcomes. Most off-face applications remain off-label, although CaHA is FDA approved for the hands and décolletage.
CONCLUSION: CaHA and PLLA provide versatile, minimally invasive options for off-face rejuvenation. Careful patient selection, anatomic knowledge, individualized technique, and realistic expectations are essential for a safe, effective treatment.

paper.title: Self-Reported Psychological Distress in Adolescent and Young Adult Idiopathic Scoliosis Patients Undergoing Posterior Spinal Fusion.
paper.summary:
BACKGROUND: Patients with scoliosis are at risk of psychological distress, which may influence outcomes following corrective surgery. Using Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS) measures, we aimed to determine the prevalence of self-reported anxiety and depression in adolescent and young adult patients preparing for posterior spinal fusion (PSF), evaluate their association with postoperative outcomes, assess overlap with pre-existing diagnoses, and examine relationships between PROMIS and Scoliosis Research Society (SRS-22r) measures.
METHODS: A cohort of patients aged 11 to 26 with adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) or young adult idiopathic scoliosis (yAdIS) undergoing PSF were retrospectively enrolled at a single academic medical center between 2019 and 2025. Patients completed PROMIS and SRS-22r instruments preoperatively and at ∼6 weeks postoperatively. Self-reported psychological distress was defined using established PROMIS T-score thresholds for anxiety and depression, while clinical diagnoses were abstracted from the medical record.
RESULTS: Of 103 patients completing preoperative PROMIS assessments, 76% (n=78) completed follow-up. Preoperative rates of self-reported depression and anxiety were 27% and 52%, respectively, compared with clinical diagnosis rates of 7% and 16%. Female sex and older age were associated with self-reported anxiety. PROMIS anxiety scores significantly improved postoperatively (Δ-3.4±8.6, P=0.001). SRS-22r self-image improved (Δ+1.1±0.8), while function (Δ-0.7±0.8, P<0.0001) and pain scores (Δ-0.4±0.9, P<0.0001) worsened postoperatively. Higher preoperative anxiety and depression scores correlated with worse postoperative pain interference, physical function, self-image, and functional SRS-22r scores, and independently predicted worse SRS-22r self-image and function after multivariable adjustment.
CONCLUSIONS: Self-reported psychological distress is prevalent among adolescent and young adult patients preparing for spinal fusion, with over half endorsing anxiety and/or depression preoperatively. Although distress improved following surgery, worse baseline anxiety and depression scores independently predicted poorer short-term functional and self-image outcomes.
LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III: retrospective cohort study.

paper.title: Serum alarin in relation to depression and anxiety in women with polycystic ovary syndrome.
paper.summary:
OBJECTIVES: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a common endocrine disorder associated with metabolic, reproductive, and psychological disturbances. Alarin, a neuropeptide of the galanin family, has been implicated in energy metabolism and insulin resistance, and experimental studies suggest a role in mood regulation. However, its association with psychiatric features in PCOS remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate circulating alarin levels in women with PCOS and their relationship with depression, anxiety, and metabolic-hormonal parameters.
METHODS: This case-control study included 180 women divided into four groups: PCOS with depression, PCOS without depression, depression without PCOS, and healthy controls (45 participants each). Clinical, biochemical, and hormonal assessments were performed, including measurement of serum alarin levels. Depression and anxiety were assessed using validated Hamilton rating scales.
RESULTS: Serum alarin levels were significantly higher in women with PCOS, irrespective of comorbid depression, compared with healthy controls and women with depression without PCOS. Women with depression alone showed alarin levels comparable to controls. Factorial analysis showed significant effects of PCOS status and depression status, with no significant PCOS × depression interaction (p=0.37). Serum alarin correlated positively with fasting insulin, HOMA-IR, and luteinizing hormone, but not with depression or anxiety severity. Multivariate analysis identified luteinizing hormone and PCOS status as independent predictors of serum alarin levels. Receiver operating characteristic analysis demonstrated excellent discriminative performance for PCOS.
CONCLUSIONS: Circulating alarin is closely associated with the metabolic and reproductive features of PCOS rather than psychiatric symptom severity, indicating a stronger link to endocrine-metabolic dysregulation.
